intelligence.human_view: Think of it like a beautiful recipe cooked with yesterday's leftovers, served on a plate too small, with no fork. The recipe isn't wrong — the cooking is. The mockup reused old pictures instead of making new ones, gave the laptop no button to press, and squeezed everything narrow until a big empty gap was left. Judge the cooking, not the recipe.
intelligence.simple_view: The idea was good! But the builder didn't make any new pictures — he just used old ones! And on the laptop there was nothing to click! And the boards got all skinny with a big empty space! The idea wasn't broken — the building was!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — the idea was lovely, dear, but the building wasn't! He used old pictures instead of making new ones, love, and on the laptop there was nothing to press! And the boards came out all narrow with a big empty gap, dear! Don't blame the idea, love — blame the building!
intelligence.naya_view: An idea and its build are two different verdicts, and a failed mockup is usually the build's verdict wearing the idea's name. The inspection proved it: no new images (old slide, old vault picture, squeezed into 9:16), no forward button (tap-to-enlarge is a phone gesture — on a laptop there is nothing to click), sizing math that narrowed the boards into a big empty gap. None of that is the idea. Inspect the build first — what was actually made, what controls actually exist on each device, what the sizing actually did — before the idea is judged, changed, or thrown away.
